excerpt: Physical Intelligence (π) builds general-purpose AI models that control robots. Its π0 to π0.7 models, open-source openpi release, Pi API beta and $5.6 billion valuation.
content:
Physical Intelligence, which writes its name as π, is a company building foundation models for robots. Its goal, in its own words, is a model that can control any robot to do any task. Its models are vision-language-action models (VLAs): they take in camera images and an instruction and output the motor actions a robot arm or mobile robot should take.

The company was founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers and academics from Stanford and UC Berkeley, SiliconANGLE reported. Karol Hausman is chief executive; Sergey Levine and Lachy Groom are also co-founders.

Its research has moved quickly. It announced π0, its first generalist policy, in October 2024, and released π0's code and weights as open source on 4 February 2025 in a project called openpi. π0.5, announced on 22 April 2025, could control a mobile robot to tidy a kitchen or bedroom it had never seen. π*0.6, in November 2025, added learning from experience with reinforcement learning, and π0.7, in April 2026, is described by the company as a steerable model with a step change in generalisation. On 13 October 2026 it opened a Pi API beta, letting outside teams upload data, fine-tune its models and run hosted inference on their own robots; access is through a waitlist.

It raised $400 million in November 2024 at a valuation above $2 billion, with Jeff Bezos, Lux Capital and Sequoia among investors, then $600 million in November 2025 at $5.6 billion, led by Alphabet's growth fund CapitalG, Bloomberg reported. In March 2026 Bloomberg reported talks to raise about $1 billion more at above $11 billion; we found no confirmation that the round closed.

There is no public pricing. The Pi API is in beta behind a waitlist, and the open-source openpi models are free to download.

This page is research, not a review: Physical Intelligence has no product we could try. It brings together Physical Intelligence's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.

fit: robotics researchers and startups that want a strong base model to fine-tune
hardware teams that want to skip building robot intelligence from scratch
anyone following the race to build robot foundation models

teams that need a supported commercial product today, since the API is still in beta

faq.a: A company founded in 2024 that builds AI models that let robots of many kinds perform many physical tasks.
Yes. Physical Intelligence released π0's code and weights on 4 February 2025 in its openpi project, which also includes π0-FAST and π0.5.

faq.q: Can I use Physical Intelligence's models commercially?
faq.a: It opened a Pi API beta on 13 October 2026 with a waitlist. No public pricing has been published.

faq.q: How much has Physical Intelligence raised?
faq.a: It raised $400 million in November 2024 and $600 million in November 2025 at a $5.6 billion valuation, led by CapitalG, Bloomberg reported.
